pr_title: [3.x] Add partial support for Android scoped storage
pr_body:
This is done by restricting read/write operations to the app specific directories. With that out of the way, we're also able to bump the target sdk version to 30!

With this change, the behavior leans closer to iOS since there, everything is saved to an app specific directory and get removed on uninstall. This may constitute a breaking change since the location of saved contents has been moved, so I'm open to feedback whether this should be cherry-picked for `3.3.x`.

In addition, we're also bumping the min sdk version to 19 as version 18 is [no longer supported by Google Play Services](https://android-developers.googleblog.com/2021/07/google-play-services-discontinuing-jelly-bean.html?m=1) and only add an additional `0.3%` of device coverage: `98.4%` -> `98.1%`.

![Android version distribution](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/914968/125147757-1a18dd80-e0e2-11eb-86bd-917a6f02f303.PNG)

Fix #38913, #45467
Revert #49436
Supersede #50332

pr_comments:
@HEAVYPOLY Seems like we may need to follow the iOS approach here and only use app specific directories.
There seem to be [a way](https://medium.com/androiddevelopers/scope-storage-myths-ca6a97d7ff37) to keep the saved data even after app uninstall, so let me know if you think that may make things easier and I'll create a separate PR for that option.

> To support the [Android storage updates](https://developer.android.com/about/versions/11/privacy/storage) (which will include enforcing [scoped storage](https://developer.android.com/training/data-storage#scoped-storage) with SDK 30, and will be required from 21 August 2021) will require a lot more work than this PR.
> 
> Scoped storage basically means that applications (that are not data management applications) will no longer be granted [`WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/Manifest.permission#WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE) permissions. To make this distinction clear, it has been replaced with the new [`MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/Manifest.permission#MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE) permission in SDK 30. With SDK 29 the revoking of `WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` permission could be delayed by setting the [`requestLegacyExternalStorage`](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/R.attr#requestLegacyExternalStorage) attribute which we did with Godot. However, with SDK 30, scoped storage will be enforced and Godot applications will no longer be granted `WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` permissions even with the `requestLegacyExternalStorage` attribute. 

Yes, I'm aware of the changes brought on by scoped storage. The current approach is a pragmatic one based on the fact the other supported mobile platform (iOS) behave similarly. As such with this approach, the mobile platforms have the same behavior, which is that files are read/written from app specific storage and removed on uninstall.

It is possible to support writing/reading from shared storage (it's obviously more work :)) so the approach here is to align the two mobile platforms first, then start the discussion on whether supporting writes/reads to shared storage is desirable. Since Godot's primary audience is game developers (with games having little need to access shared contents), having that discussion allows us to see if there's a need for this functionality, and what additional requirements it should fulfill.

> Although, we can still set the new [`preserveLegacyExternalStorage`](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/R.attr#preserveLegacyExternalStorage) permission to allow previously installed applications to continue to access data they previously had access to, which I suggest we do. Note: It will have no effect on new installs, which will be forced to use scoped storage.

This is not as straightforward as this is allowed temporarily (I suspect it'll be disabled in upcoming Android versions as well) to allow apps to migrate their data. As such we'd need to provide the ability for that data migration as well. Hence, as I mentioned, the need to discuss to see if it's needed, and figure out its requirements.

> 
> With scoped storage Godot applications will be restricted to writing to the four application specific directories:
> 
> 1. **[User files directory](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/content/Context#getFilesDir()):** currently obtained using `get_user_data_dir()`. This location and data will always be available to the application. It counts towards the application data size, is inaccessible to other applications and will be encrypted on Android 10 and above.
> 2. **[User cache directory](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/content/Context#getCacheDir()):** currently not obtainable, but should be implemented in Android now that [Expose OS data directory getter methods #48544](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/48544) has exposed `OS.get_cache_dir()`. This location is always available to the application, but Android may delete the data if available storage is low. As with the user data directory, it also counts towards the application data size, is inaccessible to other applications and will be encrypted on Android 10 and above.

This is added in this PR.

> 3. **[User external files directory](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/content/Context#getExternalFilesDir(java.lang.String)):** currently obtained using `OS.get_external_data_dir()`; therefore we should definitely not be reverting [Add OS.get_external_data_dir() to get Android external directory #49435](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/49435). This location may not be available, but if it is, the data stored there will always be available to the application. Other applications with the required permissions can access this data.

This is also exposed in this PR using the `get_system_dir(SystemDir)` method, hence why the `get_external_data_dir()` method is no longer needed.

One option here to support shared storage access would be to add additional `SystemDir` enums and support them (e.g: `SYSTEM_DIR_SHARED_PICTURES`, `SYSTEM_DIR_SHARED_DOCUMENTS`, etc...).

> 4. **[User external cache directory](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/content/Context#getExternalCacheDir()):** currently not obtainable, but should be added using, for example, `OS.get_external_cache_dir()`. This location may not be available, and if it is, Android may delete the data if available storage is low.
> 

I don't really see a need for this one, since the `get_cache_dir()` should do the job.

> This has all been available since API level 8, and has not been affected by scoped storage. Note: external storage permissions were required to access the external storage locations before API 19, but setting `minimumSDK` to 19 will solve this. All these application specific data locations are associated with the application and will be deleted when the application is uninstalled.
> 

[`hasFragileUserData`](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/application-element#fragileuserdata) allows the user to keep the app's data, albeit this only available for Android 10 and above.

> The big challenge with scoped storage that needs to be addressed is making data available to other applications i.e. the problem raised with #45467 (changing it from just requiring documentation to a bug again) and I assume the driver behind #38913. Before SDK 29, media files could be shared with other applications by saving them to the media specific sub-directories under the directory returned from [`getExternalStoragePublicDirectory()`](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/os/Environment#getExternalStoragePublicDirectory(java.lang.String)) and currently accessed using [`OS.get_system_dir()`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_os.html#class-os-method-get-system-dir). This required the `WRITE_EXTERNAL_DATA` permission that is being revoked going forward. There was another problem that was never addressed (or even raised in #45467): once the data is saved there it requires the media to be scanned (using [`MediaScannerConnection.scanFile()`](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/media/MediaScannerConnection#scanFile(java.lang.String,%20java.lang.String))) before it is available to other applications. Fortunately, this is done automatically by the device when it is rebooted, which provided a workaround, albeit a unsatisfactory one.
> 
> With scoped storage, the only way to save a file so it is available to other applications (and ensure it is not deleted when the application is uninstalled) we need to use the [`MediaStore` API](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/provider/MediaStore). With SDK 29, this is no longer restricted to just media files (Audio, Images and Video), but any type of file can now be saved to the [`MediaStore.Downloads`](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/provider/MediaStore.Downloads) collection.
> 
> Fortunately, Godot currently only provides the ability to save one time of media file: Images. An image can be saved as a PNG file using [`Image.save_png()`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_image.html#class-image-method-save-png). Unfortunately, the core code that enables this, currently uses the base `FileAccess` class to open the file that is written to:
> https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/9d4afa8b75f8db5ac039d6964c3e523119b750ca/drivers/png/resource_saver_png.cpp#L51-L70
> 
> 
> So it can’t be simply overridden in the Android inherited version:

It can be overridden. `FileAccess` (and `DirAccess`) [creates platform specific handles to open a file](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/fb3961b2ef9ed03501f98a8aa621f78679cc2be9/platform/android/os_android.cpp#L77).

> https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/9d4afa8b75f8db5ac039d6964c3e523119b750ca/platform/android/file_access_android.cpp#L44-L61
> 
> 
> Note: The Android inherited version currently doesn’t even support opening the file for writing:

The current Android version only handles `res://` paths, which by being in the Android `assets` directory are immutable at runtime.
If we decide to provide support for shared storage, then we'll need a new (java) class that'll handle all supported Godot's access type. 

> https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/9d4afa8b75f8db5ac039d6964c3e523119b750ca/platform/android/file_access_android.cpp#L51-L54
> 
> To support saving files that can be shared with other applications, we need to:
> 
> 1. Create the Java files to write the file to the appropriate `MediaStore` depending on the MIME type.
> 2. Allow the Godot Android `FileAccess` class to call this method when saving a file that should be publicly accessible.
> 3. Create the Godot interface to be able to save files to the public locations (across platforms).
> 4. Update the `ResourceSaverPNG` code to not use the base `FileAccess` class so that platforms can override it.
> 5. Optionally, create similar code to enable saving of other media files both privately and publicly.

To recap:

- This PR is a pragmatic one that adds support for scoped storage primarily for apps/games that don't need to read/write to shared storage and allows convergence of behavior between mobile platforms
- It's possible through `get_system_dir(SystemDir)` to add support for shared storage. If we decide that's a need, this can be done in a separate PR after we nail down the requirements.

Thoughts and feedback welcomed!
Saying it's not needed is effectively saying: "won't fix" #38913, #39414 and #45467.

I made no statements about your intentions. I merely pointed out the effect statements like these:

and

> If we decide to provide support for shared storage

would have in a PR that would revert the fix for #39414 and close #38913 and #45467 without properly fixing them.

I clearly laid out my thoughts on why this PR does not fix #38913 and #45467, and reverts the fix for #39414, and provided constructive feedback on how to properly fix #38913 and #45467 in my [review](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/50359#pullrequestreview-703581933). This review and its suggestions remain valid.

> I clearly laid out my thoughts on why this PR does not fix #38913 and #45467, and reverts the fix for #39414, and provided constructive feedback on how to properly fix #38913 and #45467 in my review. This review and its suggestions remain valid.

And you haven't addressed any of @m4gr3d's detailed answer to your review, and chose instead to discard it all with (indeed) a blanket statement. Whether it's *valid* or not is up for discussion and saying that it's *invalid* (i.e. that @m4gr3d's proposed pragmatic solution does not "won't fix" the referenced issues) is not an insult nor a breach of Code of Conduct.

Attempting to construe it as such seems disingenuous - and sadly it's not a first occurrence coming from you. I have to ask you *once again* to stop using this approach - which has blocked countless PRs - of giving contributors silent treatment after they replied in-depth to your own in-depth negative review.

To follow up on the points raised in the discussion here:

- Yes, this PR does not fully resolve scoped storage support for Godot on Android.
- Yes, we're still planning to add full support for it, however the implementation (and subsequent testing) is expected to take some time as it's a large refactor (anyone with a better implementation is welcome to contribute), so in the meantime, we're going with this approach in order to unblock support for SDK 30.
- Feedback and comments are welcomed so long as the above two points are taken into consideration.

Thanks!

> To follow up on the points raised in the discussion here:
>
> - Yes, this PR does not fully resolve scoped storage support for Godot on Android.
> - Yes, we're still planning to add full support for it, however the implementation (and subsequent testing) is expected to take some time as it's a large refactor (anyone with a better implementation is welcome to contribute), so in the meantime, we're going with this approach in order to unblock support for SDK 30.

That's also my understanding and the approach I recommend as we urgently need support for SDK 30 (some users are already stuck publishing new apps due to the new requirements).

I think most of the discussion on technical points boiled down to the fact that this PR says that it "adds support for Android scoped storage" and aims at closing issues which request "support for Android scoped storage". While this PR adds support for (as I understand it) scoped storage for app-specific storage, but not the full blown API.

So it's mostly a question of semantics IMO, whether we believe that supporting scoped storage means "porting existing features to use the scoped storage API" (what this PR does) or "implementing new features offered by the scoped storage API" (what should be done eventually).

I would suggest making sure that we have an issue or proposal that describes what is left to be done after the initial steps taken in this PR. I don't see any harm in doing things progressively (and that's what I advocated for both publicly and in private discussions), but I understand Marcel's disagreement with the fact that this fully implements scoped storage support for all use cases.

review_comments:
@godotengine/android @akien-mga I'm looking for feedback on this approach to easily provide support for shared and app specific storage.
For most platform, this argument doesn't make a difference (hence default to `true`). On Android (and maybe iOS), we send different paths depending on whether this is `true` or `false`.

The alternatives to this approach were either:
- Create an app specific dir enum that mirrored the `SystemDir` enum
- Or add app specific dir values to the `SystemDir` enum

I think the boolean option is fine for `3.x` (and can be forward ported to `master` too for consistency initially).

We might want to take time to rethink this API for 4.0 though, `get_system_dir()` is a very old method and it might not expose the best API to handle current features and requirements of modern OSes.

But it's also a fairly niche method that only a handful of users will need to call explicitly, which is why I think adding an Android-specific boolean flag in the short term is OK.
